description: Buying out by area (ARCHITECTURE decision 146) in a world 131072 x 98304 units (32 x 24 cells of 64 m, a cell 4096 units across, 16,777,216 square units), a managed company with $4,000,000 (400,000,000 cents), the city's buildings and footprints on, and no stations. Cells (5, 5) and (5, 6) hold homes of 48 residents and 8 jobs each: D1 (2 storeys of 1,536 m2 hold 56 residents), land worth 2,000 a m2 (a D1 home's base), so buying out either whole costs (3,072 m2 of floor at 4,000, 12,288,000, and its 20 m square's 400 m2 at 2,000, 800,000) a fifth more: 15,705,600. With buying out by area on, an office block (32 m, 2,048 units) centred on the line between the two cells, (24576, 22528), runs from 23,552 to 25,600 across and 21,504 to 23,552 down: 1,024 x 2,048 = 2,097,152 square units, an eighth, of each cell. It pulls nothing down: it pays an eighth of each cell's buy-out, 1,963,200 twice, 3,926,400, with 6,144 m2 of floor at 4,000, 24,576,000, and 1,024 m2 of land at the 2,000 of cell (5, 6), under its centre, 2,048,000: building 1, land cost 5,974,400. An eighth of each cell's people move in, rounded down: 6 residents and 1 job from each, 12 and 2, and each cell keeps 42 and 7. A house (16 m, 1,024 units) centred at (20992, 22528) lies wholly in cell (5, 5), a sixteenth of it: it pays 981,600 for the share (15,705,600 / 16), 512 m2 of floor at 4,000, 2,048,000, and 256 m2 of land at 2,000, 512,000: building 2, land cost 1,493,600. A sixteenth of 42 residents is 2 (rounded down) and of 7 jobs 0: the cell keeps 40 and 7. Both cells and their D1 buildings stay. The balance: 400,000,000 - 30,550,400 - 3,541,600 = 365,908,000. Every value worked out by hand.
